progress_update.summary: Massive design session. Squashed 42 commits into 1 on live-state-poc branch. Spent the bulk of the session developing the execution model and state graph RFC through iterative design and critique. Refined workflow state semantics (freezes on completion, result is separate return value), link primitives (status window, collections by service type, shared ownership, completion handlers, cascading GC), and workflow graph retention as a data product. Split the original RFC into three focused documents. Cleaned up the docs directory from spectre-generated task structure into a clean layout: docs/rfcs/, docs/design/, docs/plans/, docs/session_logs/.
progress_update.goal: Design the state graph and links model for Restate — making relationships between entities explicit, workflow progress observable, and computation graphs retainable as data products for learning, analytics, visualization, and reporting.

constraints: Channels design deferred until state graph is proven
Don't let RFC work block shipping the SSE POC
decisions: Workflow state freezes on completion (both success and failure). Result is a separate return value, same mechanism as today.
Links provide status window: running/success/failed + result. Completion handlers optional for flow control. Objects don't need plumbing handlers.
Workflow graph retained via link is a first-class data product (learning, analytics, visualization, reporting) — separate from the result value.
Multiple objects can link to same entity — shared ownership, ref-counted GC. Spawner not special.
Docs reorganized: docs/rfcs/ (proposals), docs/design/ (concepts/future), docs/plans/ (implementation), docs/session_logs/ (handoffs), docs/dev/ (existing)
